text:
sarah: FYI escalated from ACME — streaming responses are stopping mid-stream after their auth refresh. client shows hung SSE (no more chunks) but TCP stays ESTABLISHED. partial JSON object delivered.
chloe: ugh. any 401s in the client logs?
sarah: client shows `401` at /auth/refresh at +7s, then client retries refresh, but the SSE socket never emits close. they see last event then silence. customer says they get billed for tokens even tho model stopped streaming further tokens.
ashok: can you paste the trace? also which proxy in front (ALB / cloudflare)?
sarah: trace: frontend ALB (nginx) -> edge-proxy -> runtime. server logs show auth refresh request logged separately; runtime returned 401 to refresh but the runtime did not emit SSE `event: error` or close the connection. the connection stayed open for ~2m until client timed out.
priya: ALB idle timeout is 60s, right? but if traffic stays silent ALB may still keep it open. question: who should be responsible for terminating on failed refresh? runtime or edge-proxy?
ben: runtime should actively close on auth failure tied to session. currently we treat original SSE request as authenticated at connect, then allow token refresh path to update session. if refresh fails we mark session invalid but we don't `res.end()` for SSE. seems like a bug.
sarah: repro steps customer provided:
1) open SSE to /v1/stream with short-lived token (~12s exp)
2) let token expire; client calls /auth/refresh which returns 401
3) client expects SSE to be closed so app can re-auth and re-open
4) instead SSE stays open, app shows spinner and no new chunks

sse-monitor-bot: alert: session 0x7fb3 had token-rotate-failure; refresh 401; no disconnect recorded.
ashok: sounds like we need a deterministic behavior: on refresh failure we should send a comment ping explaining closure and then `:close` or a final SSE event and close connection. Proposal:
- On refresh 401 -> send SSE comment `: auth_failed\n` then `event: session_closed\ndata: {"reason":"auth_refresh_failed"}\n\n` then `res.end()`
- For proxies that swallow 4xx on background requests, also emit a periodic `:probe` comment every 15s to keep client-facing TCP alive until we close.
priya: agree. also add metrics: refresh_failure_disconnect_count and a breadcrumb in logs with session id.
sarah: customer also reported mobile client (iOS app) kept TCP open forever and retried refresh in a tight loop, causing billing spikes. can we add server-side rate-limiting on refresh attempts per session? maybe 3 attempts then force close.
ben: yes implement server-side backoff and final close. we should also make the behavior configurable per-tenant (some customers want auto-close, some prefer fallback to read-only stream).
ashok: small code sketch for runtime Node handler (pseudo):
```
// on auth refresh failure
res.write(`: auth_failed\n`);
res.write(`event: session_closed\ndata: {"reason":"auth_refresh_failed","retry":false}\n\n`);
res.end();
// increment metric
metrics.increment('refresh_failure_disconnect')
```
chloe: will that be visible to clients that only parse 'data' events? the comment ensures proxies like CloudFront don't cache it, but some clients ignore comments.
ashok: good point. include both comment and explicit event as above.
priya: also verify ALB / CloudFront behavior: some infra may treat trailing `res.end()` differently. add integration test in eng-infra where we simulate 401 refresh and assert TCP closed within 2s of auth failure.
sarah: customer is asking for immediate mitigation. can we deploy a small change to runtime to close sessions on refresh 401 with a rollout guard? or push a hotfix behind a feature flag.
ben: can do a canary behind `sse.force_close_on_refresh_failure` rollout. start in staging -> 10% -> 50%. add SLO alert to detect if connections spike.
chloe: also propose we add a short explanation in support reply: how to repro locally (curl) and recommend app changes: on receiving `event: session_closed` re-open flow after interactive auth. sample curl below.
sarah: paste curl repro for QA:
```
# open SSE
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <short-token>" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream
# separately simulate refresh fail
curl -X POST -d '{"refresh":"bad"}' https://api.redwood.ai/auth/refresh
```
ashok: QA checklist:
- verify runtime sends `session_closed` event and closes socket on refresh 401
- ensure comment ping cadence preserved for healthy sessions
- test proxies (ALB, CloudFront, nginx) do not swallow final event
- verify metrics increment and per-tenant config respected
priya: I'll add infra tests and an alert `sse.stuck_streams>10` for canary.
sarah: customer ok with canary; they want ETA.
ben: I'll start a PR today, canary end-to-end tomorrow, customer-facing note once canary passes. tagging @chloe for support reply draft.
chloe: thanks. rough support reply:
"We identified a case where token refresh failure didn't close SSE connections, which could leave client apps waiting for more events. We're rolling a fix to explicitly notify clients with `event: session_closed` and close the stream; we'll also rate-limit refresh attempts to avoid billing spikes. ETA: 24-48h for canary + rollout." :thumbsup:
sarah: :eyes: adding customer trace to the ticket. closing loop once canary completes.
